notes.meaning: God announces that the entire universe is His home and He rules over all of it. Since heaven is His throne and earth is merely His footstool, no human building could ever contain Him. People who took pride in the physical temple while ignoring God in their hearts failed to understand His true majesty.

The Lord made the world and everything in it, so He does not depend on human hands for anything. What catches His eye is not a grand stone building, but a person with a humble and sorrowful spirit over sin. He welcomes anyone who listens carefully and respectfully obeys His word.

When people offer religious sacrifices while choosing to live in deliberate sin, their worship disgusts God. Going through the motions of sacred rituals without genuine faith is as awful in His sight as murder, idolatry, or killing an unclean animal. God cares about the heart, not empty ceremony that masks evil deeds.

The Lord warns that He will choose the very troubles and terrors that sinners dread most. He called out to His people repeatedly through the prophets, but they refused to listen and insisted on doing evil. Because they chose what displeased Him, He will answer them with fitting judgment.

God speaks directly to the faithful believers who revere His word. Their own countrymen hated them, threw them out of the community, and mockingly dared God to show up and rescue them. The Lord promises that He will appear to bring joy to the faithful, while their persecutors will be covered in shame.

A sudden roar of battle and distress sounds out from the city and the temple. The very place where hypocrites thought they were safe becomes the center from which God carries out His justice. The Lord Himself speaks through this destruction, giving His enemies the punishment they earned.

Jerusalem is pictured as a mother giving birth suddenly and without labor pains. God's deliverance and the sudden arrival of His restored people happen far faster than normal human effort could ever accomplish. It shows how easily and swiftly the Lord can bring about new life for His church.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic tradition frequently applies this verse to the birth of Jesus, interpreting the delivery without birth pains as a sign of Mary's painless, miraculous childbirth.

notes.meaning: No one has ever heard of a whole nation being born in a single day, yet that is what God does for Zion. The rapid growth of God's people goes beyond anything seen in regular human history. In a moment, the Lord repopulates His holy city and brings forth a vast family of believers.

differ.view: Some Baptists emphasize from this verse that the church must experience deep spiritual travail and earnest prayer before souls can be born again.

notes.meaning: The Lord assures His people that He will not carry a pregnancy right up to delivery and then fail to bring forth the child. He began the work of restoring and rebuilding His people, and He has the power to finish it completely. God never leaves His promises half-done.

All who loved Jerusalem and wept over her past ruins are invited to celebrate her new life. True believers who shared in her grief can now share in her gladness. God turns the sorrow of His people into deep, lasting rejoicing.

God's children are invited to drink deeply from the comforts of the restored city, like a satisfied baby nursing from its mother. The blessings, teachings, and fellowship of God's community provide rich spiritual nourishment. Believers find true peace and contentment in what God provides.

The Lord promises to pour peace over Jerusalem like a wide, never-ending river. The wealth and honor of the surrounding nations will stream into the city to bless her. God's people will be held close, carried on the hip, and gently bounced on knees like treasured young children.

God compares His tender care to a mother comforting her grown son. When life brings sorrow, the Lord Himself will soothe His people and wipe away their grief. Believers can rest in the deep, warm love of their God in Jerusalem.

When God's people see His promises come true, their hearts will leap for joy and their strength will revive like fresh green grass after rain. The Lord will show His caring hand to those who serve Him faithfully. At the same time, His fierce anger will fall upon those who set themselves against Him.

The Lord will arrive in fiery glory, riding on storm clouds like whirling war chariots. He comes to carry out His burning anger against all unrepentant wickedness. His judgment will be swift, terrifying, and impossible to escape.

The Lord will bring His righteous judgment upon all rebellious humanity using fire and the sword. These pictures show how God uses both natural events and human history to punish evil. A great number of people who refused to turn back to God will fall under His justice.

God singles out hypocrites who go through special cleansing rites to join pagan idol worship in sacred gardens. While pretending to be holy, they openly break God's laws by eating unclean meats like pork and rats. Because they turned their backs on the true God, they will all perish together.

The Lord sees right through secret sins and knows every evil thought and action. He will bring an end to hypocrisy by gathering people from every nation and language group on earth. When they arrive, they will see His magnificent glory revealed for all to behold.

God will set up a sign among the people and send survivors across the world as His messengers. They will travel to distant regions and far-off islands that have never heard of the true God. These heralds will spread the good news of God's fame and glory everywhere.

People from all nations will bring God's scattered family back to His holy mountain in Jerusalem, using every mode of travel available, including horses, chariots, and camels. They will present these believers to the Lord as a sacred offering, brought with the same care as grain offerings carried in clean vessels to the temple. God's worldwide family will be gathered in holiness.

The Lord promises that He will choose some of these newly gathered people to serve as priests and Levites. God breaks through old tribal boundaries so that members of His renewed community can lead in worship and spiritual service. Everyone who belongs to God now has direct access to serve Him.

God promises that just as the new heavens and new earth He creates will stand forever, so the name and family of His faithful people will endure. Empires and worldly powers will fall away, but God's covenant people will never be wiped out. His promises to His children are as permanent as the new creation itself.

Worship of the one true God will become regular, continuous, and universal. People from every nation will come together to bow before the Lord week after week and month after month. The old feast days point forward to an endless life of joyful worship in God's presence.

The book ends with a solemn contrast between the blessed worshippers and the rebels who rejected God. Those who worship the Lord will see the terrible ruin of those who defied Him, whose fire is never put out and whose worm never dies. Jesus Himself quoted this warning to show the awful reality of eternal judgment.

differ.view: Many evangelicals understand the undying worm and unquenchable fire to teach that the unrepentant will suffer conscious, unending punishment in hell.
Some evangelicals believe this passage describes dead corpses being consumed until nothing remains, pointing to the final destruction of the wicked rather than everlasting torment.
